quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can your body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. Blood alcohol content (BAC) varies by person, so it is safest not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog. Once you are close to it, speed up and leave it behind. Do not kick at it.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely on your mirrors to show you all of your surroundings.
Point in the direction of the lane change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement offers the best traction.

questions.question: As you slow down or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, focus on:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. You may see part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, the group should stop.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit and then exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in their blind spot. The other vehicle could also block your escape route. Speed up or drop back.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time the rider is slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time the rider is slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is usually located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way for a rider to increase visibility?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be visible to other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light properly. Waving does not make you more visible.

questions.question: Why is riding directly alongside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver may change lanes without seeing you. Also, the other vehicle blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. If you must brake, slowly use the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road. Squeeze the clutch and stop.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever on a motorcycle is located on the left handgrip.

questions.question: What does eye contact with a driver mean?

options.text: It does not mean they will yield to you.
They will definitely yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on eye contact to mean a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not notice them.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist discourage other vehicles from lane sharing?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of a lane.
Ride in the center portion of a lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver enters your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night.
Allow a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same distance regardless of time of day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances at night because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts clearly. Allow a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make it more dangerous by encouraging them to tailgate faster.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what will happen to the steering?

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire will cause the steering to feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, leave the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle rider check their mirrors?
questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to be aware of hazards behind you.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Drive on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best response to a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them follow at a higher speed, creating more danger. Do not drive on the shoulder—other drivers do not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: Why is a leather jacket important when riding?

options.text: It makes a rider look cool.
It is usually too warm to wear.
It protects you in a crash.
It should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket, preferably leather, for protection. In hot weather, a leather jacket also helps prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm conditions.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, footwear that covers and supports the ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet. Soft material pants do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit so your arms steer the bike, not hold you up.
Sit far back so your arms stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms steer the bike, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not just hold you in place. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes a vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: In a staggered formation with multiple riders passing together.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: When a group of motorcycles passes a vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider must pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.
